chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with progression of chronic kidney disease
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 40‑year‑old male with a long‑standing history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2009, currently with stage 2 blood pressures (146/107 mmHg). Chronic kidney disease was first documented as stage 1 in 2021 and progressed to stage 2 by May 2023, accompanied by micro‑albuminuria attributed to type 2 diabetes mellitus. Although the record lists prediabetes, the patient is on insulin therapy, indicating overt diabetes. Anemia has been present since 2019, likely secondary to CKD. Recent psychosocial stress (onset May 2024) and longstanding social isolation are noted. The patient is employed full‑time and has a high‑school education. No acute visits have occurred, but wellness visits are frequent, suggesting ongoing outpatient monitoring without targeted management of his renal and metabolic disease.

risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure is markedly elevated (SBP 146, DBP 107) placing the patient in stage 2 hypertension. Chronic kidney disease stage 2 with micro‑albuminuria indicates high renal and cardiovascular risk. Anemia adds cardiac workload. Insulin use suggests overt diabetes, a major driver of CKD progression. Charlson comorbidity index is 3 (moderate complexity). Missing key labs (eGFR, lipid panel, BMI) limit precise risk quantification. Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (hypertension, CKD), renal (diabetic nephropathy), metabolic (diabetes), hematologic (anemia), and psychosocial (stress, isolation).
